subject: Re: Help using ggplot for a side by side bar graph

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Help using ggplot for a side by side bar graph
parts:
Hi:

Given your data in a data frame named cedar1,

library(reshape2)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)

cm <- melt(cedar1, id = "Quarter")
cm

ggplot(cm, aes(x = Quarter, y = value, fill = variable)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = comma)

If you want to change the default colors, try something like

ggplot(cm, aes(x = Quarter, y = value, fill = variable)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "blue"))

The melt() trick is fairly common when you want to plot multiple
variables in the same graphic. It produces two new variables:
variable, which is a factor containing the names of the measure
variables (those not in id in this case) and another named value,
which contains the values of the variables. The id variables in melt
are the ones that you want to keep as grouping variables or, more
generally, common covariates.

Since you want to plot the values, you need to use stat = "identity"
because the default stat for geom_bar() [stat_bin()] will compute
counts, and in this case you want to override it. The argument
position = "dodge" produces the side-by-side bars for the aesthetic
variable (variable, associated with fill).

Dennis
